newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks gain in active trade, seen firmer.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks gain in active trade, seen firmer.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares rose higher in active trade on Wednesday and brokers said they expected the market to continue marching ahead on strong buying after the closure of an issue by merchant bankers NMB on Thursday.
The main industrial index surged 79.59 points to close at 10,252.86, lifted by gains on several key counters.
"We are seeing some buyers in the major counters and we think this trend will continue after the NMB issue is out of the way," one broker said.
"Sentiment is quite good at the moment and the fundamentals in selected counters are looking bright," he added.
Among the day's winners, agriculture investor Chemco soared 400 cents to 4,500, wine and food producer Cairns leapt 350 cents to 1,950 and publisher Zimpapers jumped 100 cents to 4,900.

Farm-implements marker Zimplow and breweries, retail stores, hotels and soft drinks conglomerate Delta each gained 25 cents to 675 and 1,750 respectively while engineering firm Gulliver at 350 and finance house UDC at 330 both added 20 cents.
Alloys was the only loser, shedding 50 cents to 500.
Minings continued quiet but slightly firmer with Wankie Colliery five cents up at 510 while copper producer Mhangura MCM.ZI three cents off at 22.
The secondary mining index put on 1.82 points to 973.71.
